skill.name: ml-engineer
skill.description: Build and operate production ML systems using modern frameworks, serving platforms, feature engineering, evaluation, monitoring, and MLOps practices.
skill.summary: Guides production ML architecture, serving, evaluation, monitoring, and lifecycle operations.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives. The first is a markdown reference to a resource file, and the second is a recommendation systems capability statement. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or unsafe execution behavior was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.
- Recommendation systems: collaborative filtering, content-based, hybrid approaches

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 26 uses markdown backticks around a resource path, not Ruby or shell command execution. The instruction only asks the assistant to open a local documentation file when examples are needed.
Line 111 describes recommendation systems as an ML application area. It does not request system reconnaissance, host discovery, credential collection, or other security-sensitive behavior.

content.value_statement: Production ML systems are hard to deploy, monitor, and scale reliably. This skill guides model serving, feature engineering, testing, and MLOps workflows.
actual_capabilities: Design model serving architectures using FastAPI, gRPC, TensorFlow Serving, TorchServe, MLflow, or BentoML.
Plan feature engineering and feature store workflows for batch and real-time predictions.
Recommend training, evaluation, and optimization patterns for PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, and classical ML.
Define monitoring for drift, data quality, latency, throughput, and model performance.
Outline A/B tests, canary releases, rollback plans, and continuous training loops.
limitations: It provides guidance and generated plans; it does not train models without a runnable project and data.
Cloud-specific designs need account limits, security rules, and cost targets from the user.
Performance estimates require validation with real traffic, hardware, and production data.
It cannot replace legal, privacy, or compliance review for regulated ML systems.

use_cases.title: Plan resilient model serving
use_cases.description: Design serving APIs, autoscaling, monitoring, and rollback paths for production inference workloads.

use_cases.title: Move experiments to production
use_cases.description: Convert model research into reproducible pipelines with testing, versioning, and deployment checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Evaluate ML infrastructure choices
use_cases.description: Compare serving platforms, feature stores, cloud services, and monitoring tools against business constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a model deployment
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for production deployment guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me deploy a trained classification model. Ask for missing context, then propose a serving architecture, monitoring plan, and rollout checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Design a feature pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for batch and real-time features.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a feature pipeline for my ML use case. Include data validation, feature store choices, freshness targets, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize inference latency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my inference workload and propose latency improvements. Cover batching, quantization, caching, hardware choices, and measurement methods.

prompt_templates.title: Review an MLOps architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for end-to-end production review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this ML platform design for production readiness. Check training, deployment, monitoring, governance, cost, reliability, and security gaps.

output_examples.input: Design a real-time recommendation service for high-volume traffic.
output: A serving architecture with online features, model cache, API layer, and autoscaling boundaries.
A rollout plan covering canaries, A/B testing, monitoring, and rollback triggers.
A reliability checklist for latency, throughput, stale features, and degraded model behavior.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing model that has rising latency and possible drift.
output: A triage plan for latency metrics, data freshness, feature distributions, and model performance.
Optimization options such as batching, quantization, caching, and hardware review.
Monitoring updates for drift alerts, business metrics, and retraining thresholds.

best_practices: Start with reliability, monitoring, and rollback requirements before choosing model complexity.
Version data, features, models, and serving configurations for reproducible releases.
Validate offline metrics, online behavior, fairness, and business impact before full rollout.
anti_patterns: Deploying a model without drift monitoring, alert thresholds, or fallback behavior.
Treating notebook experiments as production services without tests or dependency control.
Optimizing accuracy while ignoring latency, cost, privacy, and operational support.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code?
faq.answer: It can draft implementation plans and code-oriented guidance. Review and test all generated code in your own environment.

faq.question: Which ML frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, Hugging Face, and common serving tools.

faq.question: Can it help with model monitoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan drift detection, data quality checks, latency metrics, performance alerts, and retraining triggers.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace an ML platform team?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure decisions, plans, and implementation work, but teams must validate systems in production.

faq.question: What inputs improve the answers?
faq.answer: Provide model type, traffic patterns, latency goals, data sources, cloud environment, compliance needs, and current bottlenecks.
